TecsackSoftwaredeliversprojectsthroughastructuredbutflexiblemethodologybuiltaround
fourphases:Discovery,IntegrationDesign,IncrementalDelivery,andResponsibleRollout.The
samemethodologyapplieswhethertheengagementisaplatformbuild,anAI/RAGintegration,
or a modernization project — only the specifics of each phase change with the project's scope.

Theapproachisdesignedaroundoneprinciple:shipaworkingcapabilityagainstrealdataearly,
then iterate — rather than a long build cycle before anything is usable by the client.

PHASE 1

Section: Table of Contents > 1. Overview > Discovery

Purpose

Understand the client's existing systems, data, and the specific workflow or pain point that needs to be
addressed before any design or development work begins.

What Happens

• Review of the existing platform: backend, frontend,mobile apps, and how they currently interact

• Identification of available data sources (documents,databases, APIs, third-party systems)

relevant to the project

• Stakeholder conversations to define the specificproblem being solved, not just the requested

feature

• Assessment of authentication, security, andcompliance constraints already in place

• Definition of success criteria for the engagement

Typical Outputs

– A clear problem statement and scope

– An inventory of existing systems and data sources

– Initial risk and constraint list (security,compliance, data quality)

PHASE 2

Section: Table of Contents > 1. Overview > Integration Design

Purpose

Define exactly where new capability fits into the client's existing systems, rather than designing a parallel
system that needs to be integrated later.

What Happens

• Decide where new endpoints sit within the existingAPI (business logic, auth scopes, versioning)

• Define what data needs to be indexed, connected,or synchronized (e.g., a vector database for

RAG, a new ERP integration)

• Identify which existing services or businesslogic can be reused rather than rebuilt

• Define guardrails required before real datais used: access control, data masking, logging

• Produce an architecture plan showing how presentation,API/orchestration, and data/AI layers

connect

Typical Outputs

– Integration architecture diagram

– Data flow and access-control plan

– Technical design document for the specificcapability being built

PHASE 3

Section: Table of Contents > 1. Overview > Incremental Delivery

Purpose

Get a working version of the capability in front of the client against real data as early as possible, then
refine it through short iterative cycles rather than one long build.

What Happens

• Agile, iterative development in manageablestages

• Continuous feedback incorporated as requirementsevolve

• Testing integrated throughout development,not only at the end

• Dedicated project team assembled based on engagementcomplexity: developers, technical

resources, and project coordinators

• Regular check-ins aligned with the client'sworking hours, supported by Tecsack's distributed

delivery teams for broader time-zone coverage

Typical Outputs

– Working increments delivered on a recurringcadence

– Updated backlog reflecting client feedback

– Test coverage for delivered functionality

PHASE 4

Section: Table of Contents > 1. Overview > Responsible Rollout

Purpose

Ensure a feature is safe, monitored, and access-controlled before and after it reaches real users — not
just functionally complete.

What Happens

• Access control review, consistent with theplatform's existing auth model (e.g., JWT-based

scoping)

• Data-privacy review, including masking or filteringof sensitive data before it reaches any AI/LLM

provider where required

• Monitoring and logging put in place for auditabilityand troubleshooting

• Staged rollout to real users rather than asingle full-scale launch where appropriate

Typical Outputs

– Production-ready, access-controlled feature

– Monitoring and audit logging in place

– Rollout plan and post-launch review checkpoint
